children: Another major earnings week is ahead, with NVIDIA taking center stage alongside some of the biggest names in retail, Chinese technology, cybersecurity, industrials, and global shipping. The results are set to offer fresh insights into AI spending, consumer resilience, global trade, and the direction of corporate investment.

is the week’s biggest event, with its Q3 results arriving amid an extraordinary leadership shake-up. CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and the appointment of CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO have added uncertainty to the AI investment story, sending shares sharply lower and raising questions about the company’s strategic direction and its role in financing parts of the AI infrastructure ecosystem.

Investors will be looking for reassurance that demand for its AI chips remains strong, its growth outlook is intact, and the leadership transition will not disrupt its competitive position. The results are also likely to be a major test of sentiment toward the broader AI trade.
The technology slate also features Alibaba
, offering a read on China’s e-commerce, cloud, AI, and electric vehicle markets. Palo Alto Networks
add cybersecurity, financial software, data analytics, and communications technology to the mix.
Retail will be another major focus, with Walmart

reporting against a backdrop of evolving consumer spending patterns and price sensitivity. Their results could shed light on discretionary demand, value-oriented shopping, home improvement activity, and the resilience of household budgets.
Beyond technology and retail, Walt Disney
will offer perspectives on entertainment, streaming, and food demand. Shipping companies ZIM Integrated Shipping Services
will provide updates on freight markets and global trade.
will bring lithium, hydrogen, power infrastructure, and drone technology into focus. Jumia Technologies
will add an emerging-market e-commerce perspective, while other smaller-cap names round out the lineup.

With NVIDIA’s leadership transition adding a new dimension to the AI investment debate and major retailers providing a key read on the consumer, next week’s results could offer important clues on where demand remains resilient, which growth engines are holding up, and how companies are navigating an increasingly uncertain market environment.
Below is a rundown of major quarterly updates anticipated in the week of November 16 to November 20:

is set to report its FQ3 2026 results before Monday’s U.S. market open, with investors focused on whether rapid growth in its AI cloud business can offset continued weakness in its legacy online advertising operations.

In Q2, revenue declined 4% Y/Y to RMB 31.3B (approximately $4.62B), while non-GAAP EPS of RMB 7.22 per ADS ($1.06) missed estimates. Online marketing revenue fell 19% to RMB 13.1B, reflecting pressure on the traditional advertising business. In contrast, AI-powered business revenue increased 25% to RMB 12.5B, accounting for approximately half of Baidu General Business revenue. AI Cloud Infrastructure revenue surged 50% to RMB 7.3B, with GPU Cloud revenue climbing 283%. Apollo Go completed approximately 1M fully driverless rides during the quarter, expanded to 28 cities, and surpassed 23M cumulative rides.

Management cautioned that online marketing would remain under pressure in the second half as users increasingly shift toward AI chatbots, while signaling that AI cloud infrastructure growth could accelerate. Shares fell more than 10% following the results.

Recent developments have added another layer of uncertainty for investors. A securities class action was filed on behalf of investors who purchased Baidu securities during the specified class period, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 13. The ADS has also retreated substantially from its January high of $162.52, losing more than $71.

Investors will look for evidence that AI monetization and cloud demand are gaining enough scale to offset advertising weakness while monitoring the company's autonomous-driving expansion and potential legal exposure.
Wall Street rates Baidu a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating system assigns it a more cautious Hold.
Baidu surpassed EPS expectations in 6 of the last 8 quarters, missing revenue expectations thrice in that time frame.
is set to report its FQ3 2027 results after Tuesday’s close, with investors assessing the strength of AI demand amid an unprecedented leadership transition.

In FQ2, revenue surged 106% Y/Y to a record $96.2B, while Data Center revenue jumped 117% to $89B. Non-GAAP EPS of $2.22 beat estimates, and shares gained approximately 4.7% following the results. Management guided FQ3 revenue to $108B, plus or minus 2%, and projected a GAAP gross margin of approximately 74%, assuming no Data Center compute revenue from China. It also indicated that it expects revenue growth of roughly 70% in FY2028.

Recent developments have centered on the abrupt departure of Huang. The board launched an independent investigation before accepting his resignation, while Republican lawmakers also sought a briefing from the longtime CEO.

Colette Kress was named interim CEO while retaining her CFO role, and Harvey Jones became the company's first board chair. The board is searching for a permanent successor from both inside and outside the company, while emphasizing that operations, customer commitments, and the product roadmap will continue without interruption.

The leadership uncertainty triggered a sharp selloff in the shares. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo described the resignation as a potential “one-time clearing event” for the stock. Investors will look for reassurance on strategic continuity, execution, and the outlook for AI infrastructure demand, alongside updates on margins and the next phase of product growth.
Wall Street rates NVIDIA a Strong Buy, a view shared by Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating system.
NVIDIA has beaten both EPS and revenue estimates in each of its last 8 quarters.

is set to report its FQ4 2026 results before Tuesday’s market open, with investors focused on the company’s FY2027 outlook. The stock is trading near its 52-week high, reflecting improving profitability across its businesses and expectations for further earnings growth.

In FQ3, revenue increased 7% Y/Y to $25.25B, adjusted EPS rose to $2.06 from $1.61 a year earlier, and total segment operating income climbed 21% to $5.6B. Experiences revenue grew 10% to $9.97B, while operating income increased 20% to $3.02B. Domestic Park attendance rose 3%, and per capita spending advanced 4%. Streaming operating income more than doubled to $712M. Management forecasted FQ4 segment operating income of approximately $4.9B, including an estimated $600M contribution from the 53rd week, while flagging continued softness at its Shanghai and Hong Kong parks. For FY2026, Disney expects adjusted EPS growth of 12% excluding the extra week and 16% including it and is targeting another year of double-digit adjusted EPS growth in FY2027, excluding the additional week.

Recent developments have focused on cost discipline and the evolution of Disney’s streaming strategy. Reports that the company may eliminate thousands of jobs have raised expectations of further efficiency gains, with analysts suggesting a leaner cost base could strengthen earnings potential. Disney+ is also reportedly planning to expand its creator-content offering and introduce a free tier in 2027.

On the analyst front, Citigroup and Morgan Stanley raised their price targets to $140 and $133, respectively, while maintaining bullish ratings. Investors will look for details on FY2027 earnings growth, streaming profitability, cost savings, and trends across the parks business.
Wall Street rates Disney a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating system assigns it a more cautious Hold.
Disney has beaten EPS estimates in straight 8 quarters and revenue expectations in 5 of those reports.

is set to report its FQ3 2026 results before Wednesday’s market open, with investors seeking that traffic-led sales growth can be sustained. After two consecutive quarters of improving traffic and comparable sales, expectations are higher, with the stock trading near its 52-week high.

In Q2, net sales increased 5.3% Y/Y to $26.54B, while comparable sales rose 3.8%, driven by a 3.6% increase in traffic. Digital comparable sales grew 8.7%. GAAP EPS of $4.11 included a $1.65 benefit from $994M in tariff refunds, putting adjusted EPS excluding the benefit at $2.46. Management raised its full-year net sales growth outlook to approximately 5% and EPS guidance to $9.90–$10.90, including the tariff refunds, while excluding any additional refunds from its outlook. Target also indicated that it could resume share repurchases in the second half, subject to business performance and credit-rating considerations.

Recent developments have focused on holiday merchandising and the sustainability of sales momentum. Target unveiled its holiday lineup, featuring more than 8,000 new gifts, over half of them exclusive, alongside AI-powered shopping features and daily deals running through the holiday season.

Analyst views remain mixed. Evercore ISI lowered its price target to $165 from $170 with an In Line rating, while JPMorgan and BofA raised their targets to $163 and $141, respectively, but maintained Neutral and Underperform ratings, citing concerns that comparable sales growth may prove difficult to sustain into 2027. Guggenheim, by contrast, reiterated a Buy rating and $175 price target. Investors will look for continued traffic growth, holiday demand trends, margin performance, and updates on the company's ability to maintain its sales recovery.
Wall Street rates Target a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating system assigns it a more cautious Hold.
Target has beaten EPS estimates in 6 of its last 8 quarters and revenue estimates in 50% of those reports.

is set to report its FQ2 2027 results before Thursday’s market open, with investors weighing accelerating cloud growth against a prolonged earnings shortfall. The company has missed earnings expectations in 6 consecutive reports, raising the stakes for evidence that AI and cloud investments are translating into stronger profitability.

In Q1, revenue rose 9% Y/Y to RMB 269B. AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue grew 45% to RMB 48.4B, its highest level in 22 quarters, while AI-related product revenue exceeded RMB 12B for a 12th consecutive quarter of triple-digit growth. China Quick Commerce revenue increased 45% to RMB 53.3B, although customer management revenue declined 7%. Adjusted EBITDA fell 30% to RMB 27.3B, net income dropped 75% to RMB 10.4B, and adjusted EPS of RMB 8.52 per ADS missed estimates by approximately 21%. Alibaba had deployed RMB 190B of its planned RMB 380B three-year AI investment budget by June and is targeting RMB 100B in external cloud revenue by 2030.

Recent developments have reinforced the company's push into AI and cloud services. Apple said Apple Intelligence would launch in China in December using Alibaba’s Qwen model, helping lift BABA shares approximately 6% on November 2 and contributing to a roughly 12% gain over the week. Alibaba also announced plans to provide cloud and AI services for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games and launched Qovest, an AI workspace for institutional investors.

More recently, QwenWork subscription packages reportedly sold out within 30 minutes on Singles’ Day. Investors will look for continued momentum in AI cloud demand and quick commerce, while assessing whether revenue growth can improve profitability and reverse the recent pattern of earnings misses.
Wall Street rates Alibaba a Strong Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating system assigns it a more cautious Hold.
Alibaba has missed EPS estimates in 6 of its last 8 reports, and revenue estimates 5 times in that span.

is set to report its FQ3 2027 results before Thursday’s market open, with investors looking for evidence that market-share gains are translating into stronger earnings growth. With the stock approaching a $1 trillion market valuation, expectations are high, particularly around comparable sales, margins, and the company’s ability to sustain its price investments.

In Q2, revenue rose 5.9% Y/Y to $187.9B, while adjusted EPS of $0.81 beat estimates. However, U.S. comparable sales increased 2.6% excluding fuel, falling short of expectations. Management raised its full-year net sales growth outlook to 4%–5% in constant currency but guided for Q3 adjusted EPS of $0.62–$0.64 and net sales growth of 3%–3.75%, disappointing Wall Street. Shares fell approximately 6% in premarket trading following the report.

Recent developments have centered on Walmart’s holiday pricing strategy and analyst expectations. The company announced three holiday shopping events running from November 12 through December 2, featuring more than 11,000 price rollbacks, supported in part by $2.9B in tariff refunds. CEO John Furner said Walmart was “investing heavily in price” to drive market-share gains.

Analysts’ sentiment has also improved: UBS raised its price target to $149 from $130, JPMorgan to $145 from $125, BofA to $139 from $126, and Mizuho to $135 from $125. BofA expects Walmart to update its full-year guidance toward the upper end of its previous range. Shares most recently closed at $125.67. Investors will focus on comparable sales momentum, the impact of price investments on margins, holiday demand, and whether management raises its full-year outlook.
Wall Street rates Walmart a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating system assigns it a more cautious Hold.
Walmart has beaten EPS estimates in 7 of its last 8 quarters and revenue expectations in 6 of those reports.
